short: The fall of the British stronghold of Singapore to Japanese forces, considered the worst disaster in British military history.
full:
From 8 to 15 February 1942, Japanese forces launched an assault on the British stronghold of Singapore. Defended by British, Indian, and Australian troops, the island fortress was widely considered impregnable. However, the Japanese bypassed its heavy seaward defenses by advancing rapidly down the Malayan Peninsula through dense jungle terrain, attacking from the north where the defenses were weakest.

Despite having numerical superiority, the Allied forces suffered from poor leadership, lack of air support, and rapidly depleting water supplies. On 15 February, Lieutenant-General Arthur Percival surrendered to General Tomoyuki Yamashita. Over eighty thousand British, Indian, and Australian troops became prisoners of war. The fall of Singapore dealt a devastating blow to the prestige of the British Empire and exposed Australia to the threat of invasion.
